title: Explicit Values
author: TextSavvy
summary: This article offers a multi-pronged case for leaning toward explicit instruction that does not depend on agreement with any particular curriculum or pedagogical trend. Explicit instruction does enormous communicative work in the world every day; it should be planned for obsolescence, but that is a reason to design it carefully, not to abandon it. When students are centered on explicit teaching, it forms the starter community of belonging — everyone accesses the same content, the teacher-elder speaks for a shared community of meaning. Research shows explicit instruction outperforms inquiry as a base, particularly for novices. The author challenges the assumption that withholding direct instruction is philosophically sophisticated, arguing it requires extraordinary justification when applied indiscriminately: making students 'productively struggle' to discover everything is not a default philosophy but a high-cost choice that can widen gaps between students.
points: Explicit instruction does enormous communicative work in the world and should be treated as a legitimate baseline, with planned obsolescence built in — not abandoned on principle but designed to release learners toward independence.

When students are centered on explicit teaching, it forms the starter community of belonging: everyone accesses the same content, seeing themselves as equally participating and having the same access.
Explicit instruction works better than inquiry as a base — the research across labs, classrooms, and a wide array of subjects is described as practically settled.

The assumption that withholding direct instruction is more sophisticated requires extraordinary justification; indiscriminately making students discover everything is not a default philosophy — it is a high-cost choice.
Explicit instruction creates a 'central structure' — one shared channel of content — that is both the foundation of learning and the hearth around which a classroom community forms.
quotes: the prime directive of explicit instruction should be planned obsolescence, at all scales. Explicit instruction programs need to show that their 'explicitizing-ness' knows principled bounds
when students are centered on the teaching, that forms the starter community, that forms initial belonging. You have to belong to something. You don't just have 'belonging.'
The teaching and the teacher(s) are the hearth(s) of learning. Community forms, in the beginning, when everyone sees that they're all basking in the same light and heat.
it has been found to work better as a base than inquiry. That matter is practically settled in the research (lab, classroom, wide array of subjects, interdisciplinary convergence).

A very strange way to think about it would be to wonder how you could make students productively struggle to discover what a pineapple is. That 'extraordinary' way of thinking requires extraordinary justification.
explicitness is valued in people. We don't typically like people who seem to 'play games' with information, especially unnecessarily.
This classroom has one channel, and you're on it. That's the central structure, audible and visible, and you have to have a central structure.
